speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. I am Dr. Agent; I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. To determine the cause, please tell me how many days you have had this lesion and if you have noticed any fever or chills. Additionally, have you had any recent insect bites, trauma to the area, or a history of ulcers?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ecthyma Gangrenosum (likely secondary to Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia given the necrotic ulcer, ant bite trigger, and significant immunocompromise from Crohn's, diabetes, and prior steroid use).
